Unus autem ex illis, qui erat primus, sic ait: Quid quæris et quid vis díscere a nobis? Paráti sumus mori, magis quam pátrias Dei leges prævaricári.
Irátus ítaque rex jussit sartágines et ollas ǽneas succéndi. Quibus statim succénsis,
Jussit ei qui prior fúerat locútus, amputári linguam, et, cute cápitis abstrácta, summas quoque manus et pedes ei præscíndi, céteris ejus frátribus et matre inspiciéntibus.

At ille respóndens pátria voce, dixit: Non fáciam. Propter quod et iste, sequénti loco, primi torménta suscépit.

responsory.text: Refúlsit sol in clípeos áureos, et resplenduérunt montes ab eis:
Erat enim exércitus magnus valde et fortis: et appropiávit Judas et exércitus ejus in prǽlio.

It came to pass also, that seven brethren, together with their mother, were apprehended, and compelled by the king to eat swine's flesh agai…

Matins · Tuesday, 20 October 2026

Tuesday of the Twenty-first Week after Pentecost

Feria Tertia infra Hebdomadam XXI post Octavam Pentecostes · Feria

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

Lesson from the second book of Machabees

2 Mac 7:1-4

It came to pass also, that seven brethren, together with their mother, were apprehended, and compelled by the king to eat swine's flesh against the law, for which end they were tormented with whips and scourges. But one of them, who was the eldest, said thus: What wouldst thou ask, or learn of us? we are ready to die rather than to transgress the laws of God, received from our fathers. Then the king being angry commanded fryingpans, and brazen caldrons to be made hot: which forthwith being heated, He commanded to cut out the tongue of him that had spoken first: and the skin of his head being drawn off, to chop off also the extremities of his hands and feet, the rest of his brethren, and his mother, looking on.

℟. Our enemies are gathered together, and make their boast of their own strength. O Lord, break their power, and scatter them * That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!

℣. Scatter them in thy strength, and destroy them, O Lord our Shield.

℟. That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!

Lesson II

2 Mac 7:5-6

And when he was now maimed in all parts, he commanded him, being yet alive, to be brought to the fire, and to be fried in the fryingpan: and while he was suffering therein long torments, the rest, together with the mother, exhorted one another to die manfully: Dicéntes: Dóminus Deus aspíciet veritátem, et consolábitur in nobis, quemádmodum in protestatióne cántici declarávit Móyses: Et in servis suis consolábitur.

℟. Be ye not afraid of the assault of the enemy; remember how our fathers were delivered. * Now, therefore, let us cry unto heaven, and our God will have mercy upon us.

℣. Remember His marvellous works that He hath done unto Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea.

℟. Now, therefore, let us cry unto heaven, and our God will have mercy upon us.

Lesson III

2 Mac 7:7-8

So when the first was dead after this manner, they brought the next to make him a mocking stock: and when they had pulled off the skin of his head with the hair, they asked him if he would eat, before he were punished throughout the whole body in every limb. But he answered in his own language, and said: I will not do it. Wherefore he also in the next place, received the torments of the first.

℟. The sun shone upon the shields of gold, and the mountains glistered therewith; * And the army of the heathens was spread abroad.

℣. For the army was very great and mighty then Judas and his host drew near and entered into battle.

℟. And the army of the heathens was spread abroad.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And the army of the heathens was spread abroad.

Read in Latin and English

Dominican Breviary, 1962. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).
